question: An analyst labels the advance as a five-wave impulse, as shown. Which rule of impulse waves does this count break?
options: Wave 4 has entered the price territory of wave 1
Wave 2 retraced more than 100% of wave 1
Wave 3 is the shortest of waves 1, 3 and 5
Wave 5 is longer than wave 3, which is not permitted

question: Count the internal swings of legs A, B and C. Wave B retraces 93% of wave A and does not exceed the start of A. Which correction is this?
options: Zigzag (5-3-5)
Regular flat (3-3-5)
Contracting triangle (3-3-3-3-3)
Expanded flat, because C ends beyond the end of A

question: Wave 5 subdivides into five waves but ends below the wave 3 high, after which price falls sharply. What is wave 5 called, and what does it signal?
options: A truncated fifth wave; it signals underlying weakness and often precedes a sharp reversal
An extended fifth wave; it signals that the trend has more to run
An invalid count, because wave 5 must always exceed the end of wave 3
A running flat in wave 4; the true wave 5 high is still ahead

question: Wave 1 = 10.0 points, wave 3 = 35.0 and wave 5 = 10.5. Which wave is extended, and what guideline does that support for the other two motive waves?
options: Wave 5 is extended; wave 3 will then be the shortest motive wave
Wave 1 is extended; waves 3 and 5 should each be 0.618 of wave 1
Wave 3 is extended; wave 5 should therefore extend as well
Wave 3 is extended; waves 1 and 5 tend toward equality in size

question: An analyst labels this advance as a five-wave impulse. Is the count acceptable?
options: No; wave 4 has entered the price territory of wave 1
No; wave 3 is the shortest of the three motive waves
No; wave 2 has moved beyond the start of wave 1, which an impulse does not allow
Yes; wave 2 may exceed the start of wave 1 when it forms an expanded flat
